title: CS-02 Resolution Time: declared formula, numerator and denominator with honest missing-data behaviour
risk: The Resolution Time figure is produced under different accounting rules - the clock stopped at the last agent message instead of at confirmed resolution - so the KPI is wrong in the direction that flatters the programme and every decision taken on it inherits the error.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.
Metric scope is fixed before measurement: numerator is cases with a confirmed resolution timestamp; denominator is not a ratio - a duration in hours with the censoring rule stated.
The dictionary entry for 'Resolution Time' (owner, unit, window, exclusion rule) is loaded read-only and is compared with the recomputation instead of being trusted.

inputs.formula: mean elapsed hours from case opening to confirmed resolution
inputs.expected_value: 15 hours (mean of the four synthetic resolved cases)
inputs.wrong_value_if_buggy: the clock stopped at the last agent message instead of at confirmed resolution
inputs.expected_boundary_behaviour: a case open at window end is right-censored and excluded, never counted as 0 hours

steps.action: Compute Resolution Time from the frozen rows in kpi_dataset.care
steps.expected: The stored aggregate reports 15 hours (mean of the four synthetic resolved cases) and records the formula, the window and the currency that produced it.

steps.action: Recompute Resolution Time independently from the raw counter rows for the same tenant and window
steps.expected: The recomputed value equals the stored value 15 hours (mean of the four synthetic resolved cases), and every numerator row lies inside the denominator scope.

steps.action: Force the empty-source variant of the metric (no qualifying row in the window)
steps.expected: The metric reports a case open at window end is right-censored and excluded, never counted as 0 hours; the display distinguishes missing source data from a measured zero.

steps.action: Read the dashboard payload and the metric dictionary entry
steps.expected: The dashboard renders the stored value with its window, coverage and source, and the dictionary names the owner, unit, numerator and denominator that the recomputation used.

assertions: Resolution Time equals 15 hours (mean of the four synthetic resolved cases) for the frozen window, recomputed from the raw counter rows with numerator scope 'cases with a confirmed resolution timestamp' and denominator scope 'not a ratio - a duration in hours with the censoring rule stated'.

A recomputation that yields the clock stopped at the last agent message instead of at confirmed resolution is detected as wrong: the stored aggregate and the independent recomputation must agree before the figure is published.
The dashboard payload for the same tenant and window carries the stored value with its window, coverage and measurement source; it substitutes neither a design target nor another metric's value.
Boundary behaviour: a case open at window end is right-censored and excluded, never counted as 0 hours; missing source data is never rendered as a measured zero.
forbidden: Stopping the clock at the agent's last message instead of confirmed resolution.
Treating one reopened case as two separate resolutions.
evidence: Case lifecycle timestamps with the resolution confirmation.
Censoring report for cases open at window end.
cleanup: Delete gov- aggregate, raw-counter and scenario rows for CS-02 after exporting the recomputation table.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
